subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Grammar Recall: present perfect and present perfect continuous; verb forms / For and since; congestion discussion; Activate Your English
outcomes: Use the present perfect and present perfect continuous
Discuss traffic congestion using these tenses

tf.s: The present perfect continuous is formed with have/has been + verb-ing.
tf.why: Yes, for example: I have been waiting.

tf.s: 'I've been waiting for an hour' shows an action that is still continuing.
tf.why: Right, the waiting has not stopped.

tf.s: 'I've lost my keys' is in the present perfect continuous.
tf.why: It is the present perfect simple: have + past participle.

tf.s: We use 'for' with a starting point, for example 'for 3 o'clock'.
tf.why: Use 'since 3 o'clock'; 'for' goes with a length of time.

tf.s: We use 'since' with a starting point in time.
tf.why: Yes, like since 2011 or since Monday.

tf.s: 'Where have you been?' is a present perfect question.
'I haven't been to Dubai for 2011' is correct.
tf.why: 2011 is a starting point, so we say 'since 2011'.

tf.s: Car ownership increased by 10% between 2013 and 2014.
tf.why: Yes, that is the figure in the lesson.

tf.s: 'Have' is used with he, she and it in the present perfect.
tf.why: We use 'has' with he, she and it.

tf.s: 'I was stuck in traffic for half an hour' uses 'for' with a length of time.
tf.why: Well done, half an hour is a length of time.

boxes.q: Complete: She has lived here ___ ten years.
boxes.why: Ten years is a length of time.

boxes.q: Choose: I ___ English for six years.
boxes.why: The action started in the past and continues.

boxes.q: Which sentence is present perfect continuous?

boxes.why: 'A long time' is a length of time.

boxes.q: What can the present perfect show?
o: A recent action with a result now
boxes.why: 'I've lost my phone' means I don't have it now.

o: too much traffic on the roads

boxes.q: Which reply fits 'Have you packed yet?'
boxes.why: The reply uses the present perfect continuous.

boxes.q: Complete: How long ___ you been learning English?

hunt.q: Too much traffic on the roads

mcq.q: Which sentence is in the present perfect simple?
o: I've been waiting for an hour.

mcq.q: What does the present perfect continuous often show?
o: An action that started in the past and is still continuing
A finished action at a stated past time
mcq.why: It focuses on an ongoing action.

o: an hour, three days, a year
a long time, ten minutes, a week

mcq.q: Choose: Traffic ___ (flood) the city centre for months.
mcq.why: It started months ago and is still happening.

mcq.q: You started waiting at 2 o'clock and it is now 4 o'clock. Which sentence is correct?
o: I've been waiting for two hours.
I've been waiting since two hours.
I've been waiting since four o'clock.
mcq.why: Two hours is a length of time, so use 'for'.

mcq.q: Complete the dialogue: 'Have you studied for the exam?' '___'
o: Yes, I've been studying all week!

mcq.q: Why is 'has been growing' used to talk about car ownership?
o: The growth began in the past and is still continuing
mcq.why: The continuous form shows an ongoing change.

mcq.q: What is the difference between 'I've been waiting for over an hour' and 'I've lost my phone'?
o: The first focuses on how long an action has continued; the second on a result now
The first is about the future

mcq.q: Car ownership rose by 10% in one year. What problem might this cause?
mcq.why: More cars usually mean more traffic.
